findings.title: Break state machine ambiguity: nested or separate phase?
findings.description: Plan does not clarify whether BREAK is a separate top-level phase or nested state within BIDDING. This affects event sequencing, timeout handling, frontend rendering, and database schema.
findings.location: Plan overview, item 1, state machine digest
findings.fix: Update plan to explicitly state: Break is a separate top-level phase with Auction.phase = BREAK. When phase is BREAK, no bids accepted. Break starts with BREAK_STARTED event, ends with BREAK_ENDED, triggering phase transition back to BIDDING.

findings.title: Break counter scope resolution: plan assumes PER_PLAYER without product sign-off
findings.description: Plan assumes break counter scope is PER_PLAYER but PRD and AGENTS.md explicitly state scope must be configurable or explicitly resolved. No documentation that this choice has product approval.
findings.location: Plan 'Assumptions and unresolved items' section, item 1; item 8
findings.fix: Before implementation: (1) Obtain explicit product confirmation on scope (PER_PLAYER vs PER_AUCTION vs configurable). (2) Update plan items 1, 2, 8, and 'Open decisions' with confirmed scope and rationale. (3) Update item 18 validation schema to validate breakCounterScope enum.

findings.title: Squad validation at settlement: exact enforcement timing unclear
findings.description: Plan defers squad validation UX to 'Phase J' but does not specify whether validation blocks settlement (error) or warns (info). Item 7 (SettlementService) assumes validation is called but lacks return type or error handling specification.
findings.fix: Confirm with product: does incomplete squad block settlement or allow completion with warning? Update item 7 to specify exact error handling. Update item 20 integration test to test both paths: blocked and warning. Move D-13 from 'deferred' to 'confirmed'.

findings.title: Frontend Socket.IO reconnect handling: strategy unspecified
findings.description: Plan items 15–16 describe Socket.IO hooks and state context but do not specify how break and squad state are reconciled on reconnect. Ambiguity on refetch vs. event-only strategy can cause inconsistent UI state.
findings.fix: Clarify: on reconnect, client must fetch current break status via GET /v1/auctions/:auctionId/breaks/current **before** subscribing to real-time events. Add to item 15: useEffect hook that refetches on socket.connected. Update item 20 integration test: disconnect during break, verify BreakTimer reconciles deadline correctly.

findings.title: Break adjustment permissions: no optimistic concurrency or idempotency strategy
findings.description: Item 4 endpoint (POST /breaks/:breakId/adjust) is host-only but lacks version check, idempotency key, or concurrent modification handling. Two simultaneous requests could collide with lost updates.
findings.fix: Add version check to adjust endpoint: POST /breaks/:breakId/adjust { adjustmentSeconds: int, expectedDeadline?: DateTime }. Backend validates expectedDeadline matches current deadline; rejects if mismatch. Update item 20 integration test: add scenario 'concurrent host adjustments', verify second request is rejected or version-validated.

findings.title: Break reason field: enum or free-text string?
findings.description: AuctionBreak.reason is a string in schema. Plan does not specify whether reasons are enumerated (e.g., 'AUTOMATIC_TRIGGER', 'HOST_ADJUSTMENT') or free-form. Frontend needs to know for localization.
findings.fix: Define enum: BreakReason = 'BID_COUNT_THRESHOLD' | 'HOST_REQUESTED'. Update item 1 to validate reason against enum. Update item 3 BreakDto to use reason enum. Document reason values and localization in item 23.

findings.title: BreakManagerService bidCounter: in-memory state lost on restart
findings.description: Plan item 1 notes BreakManagerService has private bidCounters: Map. This in-memory map is lost on server restart, causing incorrect break triggering after restart. Violates AGENTS.md § 4 requirement to persist state.
findings.fix: Remove bidCounters Map from BreakManagerService. Add method to AuctionsRepository: getBidCountForAuction(auctionId, scope): Promise<number>. Query database to count bids since last player intro (PER_PLAYER) or since auction start (PER_AUCTION). Item 8: after bid accepted, fetch count from DB. Update item 20 integration test: restart server mid-auction, verify bid counter recovers correctly.

findings.title: Squad progress initialization: idempotency and late-join scenarios unclear
findings.description: Plan item 19 says 'initialize progress on DRAFT→LIVE' but does not specify idempotency or what happens if initialization is called twice or if team joins after LIVE.
findings.fix: Update item 2 SquadsService: method initializeProgressForTeam(teamId, force=false). If force=false and progress exists, return early. Item 19: call initialization for each team on DRAFT→LIVE. Add to item 20 integration test: verify initialization is idempotent (no duplicate records).

findings.title: BreakTimer reconciliation: behavior if deadline has passed
findings.description: Plan item 11 (useBreakTimer) says 'reconciliation on every state update' but does not specify behavior if server deadline has already passed. Countdown will show negative or zero; component must handle gracefully.
findings.fix: Update item 11 implementation note: if deadline <= now, do not render timer; if phase is BREAK, fetch current auction state; if phase changed, trigger phase transition. Add to item 20 integration test: reconnect **after** break ends, verify UI transitions correctly.

findings.title: Frontend responsive layout for break overlay: mobile specifics missing
findings.description: Plan items 12–13 mention BreakScreen component but do not detail mobile-specific layout. DESIGN.md § 10 requires 'Move chat and detailed squad views into tabs/drawers' on mobile.
findings.fix: Update item 12 to specify responsive layout: Desktop (1024px+) side-by-side timer/squad; Tablet (768px) stacked; Mobile (375px) full-height timer, squad in scrollable drawer, host controls in fixed footer. Item 13: render controls as fixed footer on mobile. Add to item 21: responsive tests at 375px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px.

findings.title: Squad rule configuration: host-editable after auction start?
findings.description: Plan item 18 validates squad rules at room creation but does not state whether host can edit rules after auction starts. AGENTS.md § 4 requires audit and explicit policy for mid-auction changes.
findings.fix: Update item 18 validation note: 'Squad rules are frozen at auction start; no edits allowed after DRAFT phase ends.' Add database constraint if needed. Add to item 20 integration test: attempt to edit rules after auction start, verify rejection. Document in item 23: squad rules are immutable during auction.

findings.title: DTOs lack serialization annotations
findings.description: Plan item 3 defines DTOs but does not specify serialization (e.g., camelCase ↔ snake_case mapping). Low impact but improves code clarity.
findings.fix: Update item 3 DTO definitions to include @Expose/@Transform annotations for serialization (e.g., secondsRemaining calculation).

findings.title: Event sequence not mentioned for break/squad events
findings.description: Plan item 6–7 defines event types but does not specify how event sequence is assigned. Low impact — existing phase G likely has pattern.
findings.fix: Update item 6–7 to note: 'Break and squad events follow existing AuctionEvent.sequence pattern; sequencer increments automatically.'

findings.title: TypeScript strict mode: squad rule types incomplete
findings.description: Plan item 2 SquadsService methods do not fully specify types for squad rule parameters (role, categoryId, minCount, maxCount). Minor type clarity issue.
findings.fix: Ensure all SquadsService methods explicitly type role (PlayerRoleType | null), categoryId, minCount, maxCount parameters; avoid any.

recommendation: Resolve all HIGH findings and document answers in plan before assigning implementation tasks. Plan cannot proceed without clarifications on: (1) break phase semantics, (2) counter scope decision, (3) squad validation timing, (4) reconnect logic, (5) concurrent update handling.
